determination_table_content.details:
Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Coles Group
Limited (Coles), proposes to acquire a leasehold interest for a Coles
supermarket within a new neighbourhood centre at Clementine
Village in Upper Swan WA 6069 (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Coles, is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that
primarily operates:
• supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles
Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd; and
• retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland,
Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.
The lessor, Saracen Properties Pty Ltd is an Australian private
property development and building company. It is based in Perth,
WA.
The Target Site is in Upper Swan, WA, approximately 33km northeast
of Perth.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The leasehold interest is an input to Coles’ existing supermarket
retailing operations, which would facilitate Coles establishing the
new supermarket.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, other information provided by the parties and
publicly available sources.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The proposed Coles supermarket would face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers in the surrounding area.
• The aggregation arising from the Acquisition is not sufficient to
meaningfully change competition in the relevant local market.
• The Acquisition does not involve Coles acquiring a competitor.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

events.title: Sanad Services and Tikehau Capital–Revima - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Sanad Services Group, owned by One Hundred and Seven
Investment RSC LTD – Sole Proprietorship L.L.C. (Sanad Services)
and Ace Aéro Partenaires II S.L.P. (AAP2) (an investment fund)
propose to acquire Revima Holding SAS (Revima) (the Acquisition).
The Acquisition would result in Sanad Services and AAP2 obtaining
joint control of Revima through a joint special purpose vehicle,
Dream BidCo.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Sanad Services supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul services
for aircraft engines and related aftermarket services. Sanad Services
provides these services to customers globally from its facilities in
the UAE. Sanad Services is ultimately owned by Mubadala
Investment Company PJSC (MIC), a UAE public joint stock company
wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi.
AAP2 is an investment fund represented by Tikehau Investment
Management SAS (TIM), in its capacity as management company.
TIM is itself a wholly owned subsidiary of Tikehau Capital SCA, the
parent company of the Tikehau Capital group, a France-based global
asset management and investment group.
The target, Revima, supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul
services for aircraft auxiliary power units and aircraft landing gear
systems. Revima also supplies, to a more limited extent,
maintenance, repair and overhaul services for engine parts (but not
for complete engines). Revima services customers globally from its
facilities in France and Thailand.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Revima supplies some maintenance, repair and overhaul services for
individual engine parts.
Sanad Services supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul services
for complete engines.
Providers of engine maintenance, repair and overhaul services may,
at times, outsource such services in respect of certain individual
engine parts. However, there is no current subcontracting
relationship between Sanad Services and Revima.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market in
Australia. In reaching its decision, and based on the material before
it, the ACCC makes the following findings.
• There is minimal overlap between Sanad Services and Revima
and they are not close competitors in the supply of maintenance,
repair and overhaul services.
• Although engine parts maintenance, repair and overhaul services
may be supplied as an input to engine services, the Acquisition
would be unlikely to give rise to vertical effects, because there
are multiple alternative suppliers of both engine maintenance,
repair and overhaul services and engine parts maintenance,
repair and overhaul services. Therefore, the merged entity would
be unlikely to have the ability and incentive to foreclose rivals in
either service offering.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
NJM4 Corporation, a special purpose vehicle managed by Nojima
Corporation (Nojima), proposes to acquire an 80.1% interest in
Hitachi Global Life Solutions’ (Hitachi GLS) home appliances
business and Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances B.V. (AHHA)
(together, the Target) through a series of interconditional steps
(including Hitachi GLS’ acquisition of a 60% interest in AHHA), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).
Nojima, NJM4 Corporation and Hitachi GLS applied for a notification
waiver in respect of the Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
17 August 2026

The acquirer, Nojima, is a Japanese consumer electronics and home
appliances retailer headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo and listed on
the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Nojima is primarily engaged in the retail
of consumer electronics and home appliances through an extensive
network of stores across Japan and in Southeast Asia (to a limited
extent). Nojima does not have any retail or wholesale operations in
Australia.
The Target comprises the Hitachi-branded home appliances
business, which manufactures and supplies Hitachi-branded home
appliances globally, including Hitachi GLS and AHHA. Hitachi GLS
manufactures and sells home and commercial appliances under the
Hitachi brand, primarily in Japan. Hitachi GLS and Arçelik A.Ş.
(Arçelik), a Turkish domestic appliances and consumer electronics
manufacturer, set up AHHA, a joint venture to manufacture, sell and
provide after-sales services of Hitachi-branded home appliances
outside of Japan, including Australia. Pre-Acquisition, Arçelik holds a
60% stake in AHHA and Hitachi GLS holds the remaining 40%.
AHHA currently distributes Hitachi-branded refrigerators, washing
machines, dryers and vacuum cleaners in Australia. Hitachi GLS
does not have any presence in Australia separate from AHHA.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Nojima and Hitachi
GLS (including its connected entities) or between Nojima
and AHHA in the manufacture and supply of refrigerators,
washing machines, dryers or vacuum cleaners in Australia
b. there are alternative manufacturers and suppliers of
refrigerators, washing machines, dryers and vacuums in
Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct in Australia
post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

events.title: Obayashi Corporation - Multiplex - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Obayashi Corporation (Obayashi)’s proposed acquisition, via its
subsidiary, of 100% of the shares in BCI UK Holdings Ltd which,
together with its subsidiaries, makes up the Multiplex Group
(Multiplex) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Obayashi, is a Japanese construction contractor that
carries out and participates in building construction, infrastructure
development and renewable energy projects in Japan and
elsewhere, including in Australia. Obayashi is involved in the
development of large-scale projects including stadiums, mixed-use
developments, and transport infrastructure. In Australia, Obayashi
participates in certain large-scale construction projects through an
arrangement with Built Pty Limited, an Australian construction
company.
The target, Multiplex, is a construction company that supplies
building construction services across Australia, Canada and the UK.
In Australia, Multiplex’s services primarily involve the delivery of
large-scale construction projects, including high-rise developments,
across sectors such as commercial offices, retail, health and social
infrastructure.

Obayashi and Multiplex (together, the Parties) both supply building

determination_table_content.details:
AbbVie, Inc, via its wholly owned subsidiary Andor LLC (together,
AbbVie), proposes to acquire 100% of the outstanding shares in
Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. (Apogee) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, AbbVie, is a North Chicago-based, New York Stock
Exchange-listed global biopharmaceutical company active in the
development and supply of medicines and therapies across a range
of therapeutic areas, including immunology, oncology, neuroscience,
aesthetics and eye care.
In Australia, AbbVie supplies Rinvoq, a Janus Kinase inhibitor used
to treat atopic dermatitis.
The target, Apogee, is a San Francisco-based, NASDAQ-listed
clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing a
pipeline of biologic therapies for inflammatory and immunological
diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, eosinophilic
oesophagitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Apogee’s lead asset, zumilokibart (APG777), is a clinical-stage
(Phase 2b) monoclonal antibody therapy that targets interleukin-13
(IL-13) for the treatment of atopic dermatitis. Apogee does not have
any marketed products anywhere in the world.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
AbbVie and Apogee overlap in the research and development of
therapies for the treatment of atopic dermatitis.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information, as relevant.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Rinvoq and APG777 are unlikely to be close substitutes,
given their differentiated mechanisms of action, safety
profiles, onset of action and methods of administration.
• There are other competitors who already supply, or are
active in the development of, atopic dermatitis therapies that
will continue to compete with the merged entity.
• The potential competition between the Parties in relation to
other pipeline products for the treatment of atopic
dermatitis is uncertain, given the early stages of the Parties’
respective pipeline products.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

VSA Roads Pty Ltd (VSA) proposes to acquire the assets of

VSA supplies quarried and bituminous products, together with
specialist contract paving and bituminous surfacing services
(including spray sealing and line marking services) across South
Australia, Victoria, New South Wales, and the Northern Territory.
SprayLine supplies bituminous spray sealing, line marking, and road
maintenance services across Victoria, New South Wales, and South
Australia. The Victorian Government has decided to no longer
operate an internal road maintenance provider, which has resulted in
a decision to divest SprayLine's spray sealing and line marking
business. The Acquisition relates only to the spray sealing and line
marking activities of SprayLine.
The reasons for the ACCC’s determination are set out in section 2.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the acquisition, market feedback and publicly available information.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect. Determination | VSA - Sprayline (MN - 30032)
Overlap and relationship between the Parties

VSA and SprayLine (the Parties) overlap in the supply of line marking and spray sealing services. VSA provides these services across South Australia, Victoria, New South Wales, and the Northern Territory. SprayLine supplies these services in Victoria, and, to a limited extent, in South Australia.

In respect of line marking services, the overlap between the Parties is limited as VSA has only a small presence in the supply of these services. SprayLine has a greater presence in line marking, driven primarily by services provided to the Victorian State Government. There is very limited overlap in terms of the customers to which the Parties supply line marking services.
Industry background

Spray sealing is a road surfacing treatment that is generally a cheaper option compared to asphalt for medium and lightly trafficked roads. It is commonly (but not exclusively) used in regional areas. Spray sealing is completed by spraying a narrow film of bituminous binder onto a street surface and then covering it with a layer of aggregate. The bituminous binder acts as a waterproofing layer and prevents water entering the underlying road structure.

Most spray sealing work is undertaken for state and local governments, although there are also private sector customers (for example, for a privately-owned carpark, airport or road). Spray sealing work for local and state governments is generally completed through tender processes, including through the following processes which are specific to Victoria:

items: State government tender processes for Victorian road maintenance contracts (VRMCs) in 8 regions of Victoria, which (among other things) provide successful VRMC suppliers a right to tender for certain planned maintenance works, which may include spray sealing, in their allocated region.

State government tender processes for planned spray sealing works in a particular region, potentially for the duration of the spray sealing season (in Victoria, this is usually the period from November to March). These tenders are open to any provider, including (but not limited to) VRMC suppliers.
Collective or individual tenders from local councils in respect of spray sealing work required to be performed in the relevant local government area(s) for a particular period (often 1-2 years).

Tenders for panels maintained by bodies including Procurement Australia and the Municipal Association of Victoria (MAV).1 Inclusion on one of these panels, means a panel firm can be contracted by a local government requiring spray sealing works at agreed rates rather than conduct their own tender process. These panels can remain active for several years with multi-year extensions. 1 The legislated peak body for local councils in Victoria. Determination | VSA - Sprayline (MN - 30032)

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Spray sealing is a seasonal activity, requiring dry weather. As spray sealing equipment is mobile, firms can move equipment around the country to perform works in different parts of Australia to maximise the utilisation of their assets.
Competition assessment

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed.

The ACCC has considered whether the Acquisition is likely to substantially lessen competition by reducing competitive constraint which would enable the merged entity to raise prices, reduce output or degrade the quality of its spray sealing or line marking service offerings post-merger.
The ACCC’s assessment is set out below.
Relevant areas of competition

The ACCC has considered the effect of the Acquisition on competition in the supply of spray sealing services and line marking services. In terms of the geographic area in which competition has been assessed, the ACCC’s assessment has focused on Victoria, as this is where SprayLine is based and where it predominantly supplies services (although it also supplies services in South Australia). Any competition concerns arising out of the Acquisition are therefore likely to be most acute in Victoria. However, the ACCC considers the geographic market for the supply of spray sealing and line marking services may be broader, including at least some parts (and potentially the whole) of South Australia and New South Wales.

It was not necessary for the ACCC to reach a concluded view on the precise boundaries of the geographic market for the purposes of assessing the Acquisition as the adoption of a broader geographic market would not result in a different outcome of the ACCC’s assessment. Noting this, for the reasons set out in the preceding paragraph, the ACCC has focused on the impact of the Acquisition in Victoria in making this Determination.
Horizontal unilateral effects in the supply of spray sealing services

The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in relation to the supply of spray sealing services in Victoria. In reaching its decision, and based on the materials before it, the ACCC makes the following findings:

items: While VSA and SprayLine are close competitors for the supply of spray sealing services in Victoria, particularly for work tendered by the Victorian Department of Transport and Planning and some local councils (depending on their location and requirements), the ACCC considers that the merged entity would be likely to be constrained by the following factors: Determination | VSA - Sprayline (MN - 30032) o Alternative suppliers of spray sealing services are available to both state and local government customers, which would likely continue to compete with the merged entity post-Acquisition. These include major firm Fulton Hogan as well as smaller spray sealing suppliers. o The ability of local councils to exercise countervailing power by developing in-house spray sealing capabilities to both self-supply and potentially supply these services to other councils (for example, Moyne Shire Council has this capability). This is likely to constrain the merged entity in the supply of local government work. o The threat of timely new entry or expansion, particularly by:

firms already supplying broader road maintenance services to state and local government customers that have existing depot networks, workforces and access to bitumen and aggregate, of which there are many active in the relevant region in circumstances where the barriers to such firms supplying spray sealing services appear relatively low, and
firms supplying spray sealing in neighbouring states such as Boral and Downer.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Horizontal unilateral effects in the supply of line marking services

The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in relation to the supply of line marking services in Victoria. In reaching its decision, and based on the materials before it, the ACCC makes the following findings:

items: VSA and SprayLine are not close competitors in the supply of line marking services, and
multiple alternative suppliers of line marking services would remain in the relevant region post-Acquisition.

determination_table_content.details:
Golden Energy and Resources Pte Ltd (GEAR) and M Resources Pty

via a jointly owned special purpose vehicle, the assets of the
insolvent Tahmoor Colliery (Tahmoor) (together, the Parties).
Tahmoor is a coal mine in the Illawarra region of NSW.
The relevant assets include the mining rights, plant and equipment,
real estate and a 16.67% equity interest in Port Kembla Coal
Terminal Limited.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquiring entity, Golden M Tahmoor Coal Holdings Pty Ltd, will
ultimately be owned 70% by GEAR (or related entities) and 30% by M
Resources (or related entities / persons).
GEAR and M Resources are part of an existing consortium, GM3,
which operates the Appin and Dendrobium coal mines in the
Illawarra region (through Illawarra Coal Holdings Pty Ltd) and has an
existing minority interest in the Port Kembla Coal Terminal (together,
the GM3 Assets). GEAR has a 51% economic interest in the GM3
Assets and M Resources has 7%.
GEAR is a Singaporean based resources company. Its activities in
Australia involve gold mining and metallurgical (coking) coal
production, through the GM3 Assets and a 59% shareholding in
Stanmore Resources Limited (Stanmore), which produces coal in
Queensland.
M Resources is an Australian based coal trader and logistics
provider. It has interests in various businesses which service coal
mines, including Mastermyne Limited, One Rail Australia Holdings
Limited, Merald, M Critical Minerals and Stanmore. None of M
Resources businesses interact with mines in the Illawarra region
except for the GM3 Assets.
Tahmoor produces coking coal and small amounts of thermal coal
for domestic and export customers. Tahmoor has been inoperative
since late 2024 and is in liquidation.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
The Parties overlap in the production and supply of thermal and
coking coal in the Illawarra region. GM3 and Tahmoor, before it
ceased operating, both supplied coal to export customers as well as
BlueScope Steel Limited (BlueScope), based in Port Kembla.
Historically, GM3 also acquired coking coal from Tahmoor to supply
export customers.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Acquisition is unlikely to have an adverse impact on the only
domestic consumer of coking coal, taking into account long-
term supply arrangements being put in place and export
customers of coking coal have a range of alternative options.
• The aggregation in the supply of thermal coal resulting from the
Acquisition is low, and both domestic and export customers
have a range of alternative suppliers of thermal coal post-
acquisition.
• The merged entity is unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
foreclose rivals’ access to the Port Kembla Coal Terminal given
the merged entity would not have a controlling interest post-
acquisition.

representative agent solution designed to engage and
convert inbound buyers.

provider of CRM software. Its core products include:
• Intercom Helpdesk, a customer service management
solution used by human customer support agents. Its
features including an omnichannel inbox, AI-enhanced
ticketing, knowledge management, proactive customer
engagement tools, and reporting and analytics.
• Fin, an agentic AI product for customer service that typically
works on top of Intercom’s Helpdesk or another provider’s
helpdesk solution.

between the Parties

Salesforce and Intercom (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply
of CRM solutions. In particular, the Parties both offer CRM products
that provide customer service, agentic AI customer service, and
agentic AI marketing/sales agent functionality.

CRM software via API.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Relevant areas of competition
items: The extent convenience stores and small supermarkets compete with full-line supermarkets such as the Proposed Supermarket.
The extent to which consumers in Kalgoorlie routinely travel to do their grocery shopping, and how far they do so.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Potential over-supply of supermarket capacity that could induce the exit of effective competitors
items: The level of market concentration in the south/south-western end of Kalgoorlie and Kalgoorlie generally before and after the Acquisition.

The competitive offerings of each supermarket competitor in Kalgoorlie (including but not limited to price, quality, product range and service) and the intensity with which they compete in the relevant markets.
Price, quality, product range and service differentials between the major and independent supermarkets in Kalgoorlie.

The likelihood and viability of new entry and expansion in Kalgoorlie to increase competitive intensity with the Proposed Supermarket, including further consideration of suitable supermarket sites, planning and zoning requirements, and likely population growth.
The profitability of Coles and independent supermarket(s) in Kalgoorlie should the Acquisition proceed.
The impact on the level of competitive constraint imposed by existing rival supermarkets in Kalgoorlie should the Acquisition proceed.
The effect on competition should one or more competitor supermarket(s) exit following the expansion of Coles via the Proposed Supermarket.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Creating, strengthening or entrenching a substantial degree of market power
items: Whether or not Coles has, or is likely to have, substantial market power.
The likely economic rationale for Coles opening the Proposed Supermarket, including its dependence on the level and nature of future competition in the relevant market.
Whether the Acquisition is likely to reduce competitive constraint.
Whether the Acquisition would, in all the circumstances, be likely to have the effect of creating, strengthening or entrenching a substantial degree of power in the local market.
